newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Central Bank aims for 25 pct refinance rate.
newsitem.headline: Russia Central Bank aims for 25 pct refinance rate.

text.p: Russia's Central Bank aims to cut its refinancing rate to around 25 percent from a current 42 percent, chairman Sergei Dubinin said on Tuesday, but he declined to put a timeframe on rate changes.
"We will keep the refinancing rate a little higher than the market rate -- (down) to a range of 25 percent. When that will happen, I cannot say," he told a bankers' conference.

"It is dangerous to name any numbers," he added. "If we have 12 percent inflation and you add to that about five percent to get the market rate for GKO (discount Treasury bills) and maybe a bit more...that is the market level which must be used as a basis."

The Central Bank does not actually use the refinancing rate, reduced to 42 percent in February, as the basis for a lending facility to commercial banks, but the rate is seen as a key financial indicator.

Dubinin said that the rouble corridor, a soft peg to the dollar, would last until the end of the year as planned and that the Central Bank would announce further policy a month before the current one ended.
He said the bank had actively intervened on the interbank currency market over the last month. "In the last month we have bought dollars much more than we have sold," he said.
First deputy Central Bank chairman Sergei Aleksashenko on April 17 said that the bank had bought a net $1.5 billion over the previous six weeks.
